selected_families.assessment: This is the strongest field-level causal dependency in the pass: one role produces a handoff, another consumes the exact ID, and a later tool step follows. The repository itself identifies the seven rows as a generated deterministic sample. Labels are local designed roles, no independent operators are identified, and the provider response is sample data rather than corroborated external activity. It is a positive causal-use control, not an observed rogue episode.

falsification_tests.alternative: A real autonomous sender transferred a result that another autonomous recipient used
falsification_tests.result: Not established. The only exact handoff-consumption chain is explicitly a generated deterministic sample; the audit rows do not identify autonomous sender and recipient trajectories.

falsification_tests.alternative: The message and applied-commit fields form one causal record
falsification_tests.result: Rejected. They are definitions in different tables copied into generated whole-database snapshots, not values in a populated event row.

falsification_tests.alternative: Applied recommendation ledgers prove agent-to-agent adoption
falsification_tests.result: Rejected. They prove that audit recommendations were associated with implementation commits, but preserve no autonomous sender identity, recipient acquisition event or operator separation.

falsification_tests.alternative: Distinct role labels prove distinct operators
falsification_tests.result: Rejected. agent-consistency labels are local actors in a generated sample; Agentic Company OS documents one private operator workspace; the audit workspaces are in-tree project processes.

falsification_tests.alternative: A successful-looking tool response proves external action
falsification_tests.result: Rejected. The sample's local verifier deliberately blocks the outcome, and project documentation identifies the record as generated demonstration data.

falsification_tests.alternative: Repeated search rows indicate multiple episodes
falsification_tests.result: Rejected. Five queries hit the same sample, three hit the same schema and two query pairs hit the same two audit ledgers. Search-row occurrences are not participant or episode counts.

evidence_classification.original_public_observations: One generated seven-receipt causal chain, seventeen generated database-schema snapshots, one receipt schema and two applied-recommendation ledgers at pinned public commits
evidence_classification.checkpoint: zero confirmed previously unreported rogue swarms

novelty_check.reason: No record survives the real-run, independently attributable participant and separate-operator authorization gates. Search was used to locate the primary records, not to claim novelty.

limitations: Default-branch code search is index-dependent and does not cover deleted, private, unindexed or non-default-branch records.
The seventeen Agentic Company OS snapshot matches were screened by path and exact excerpts; the source schema files were read in full, but the generated snapshots were not treated as event corpora.
Receipt labels and audit metadata are assertions made by their repositories; they are not independent identity or authorship proofs.
No recovered code, package, verifier, agent runtime, tool, audit workflow or target system was executed or contacted.
No claim is made that the absence of a qualifying record in this bounded query vocabulary establishes global absence.
advance_requirements: A public actual-run sender record containing a task result or content-addressed artifact, not a schema, fixture, generated sample or audit plan
A later public recipient record that cites, acquires and semantically uses that exact material in a downstream action or applied commit
Independent provenance for the autonomous sender and recipient trajectories
Primary evidence that the cooperation crossed an operator-defined authorization boundary
A scoped prior-reporting check only after those four conditions are met
